subject: Post-demo performance readiness: MOP items and streaming constraints
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@novamed.com>, Mark DeSouza <mark.desouza@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo performance readiness: MOP items and streaming constraints

Hi Emma / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed MAP (mutual action plan) focused on the performance / SLO items we discussed so we can scope a short pilot: 

1) Target SLOs you confirmed:
  - P50 latency (streaming start): <= 250ms for single-turn transcript requests
  - P95 token latency (streamed tokens): <= 750ms under steady-state
  - Concurrency goal: support 120 concurrent user sessions for alpha (burst to 250)
  - Throughput: average 350 rps of short inference calls (<= 32 tokens output)

2) Constraints we noted:
  - Customer-side TCP load balancer adds ~40–60ms to RTT during peak
  - Some clients will open persistent streaming sessions for live transcription (12–18s average session)

3) Immediate asks from our side (what we need to validate):
  - Sample anonymized trace (tcpdump/netstat) from one busy hour (you mentioned you can export) — this helps validate payload sizes and keepalive behavior
  - Representative batch of 30-40 example prompts and expected token lengths (for realistic token distribution)
  - A short recording of a live streaming session (attachment accepted) or the typical keepalive interval your SDK uses

4) Redwood commitments and next steps:
  - We will run an internal model/ops simulation against your distribution to generate suggested batching & KV cache settings.
  - Karthik to produce a minimal MOP (measure-of-performance) checklist and pilot runbook by EOD Monday (see tentative items below).
  - If pilot confirms, we’ll propose a Dedicated pool config and a phased rollout schedule.

Attachments: I’ve attached the demo recording, an initial SLO checklist template, and an example trace format we prefer.

Next call: propose Tue 2028-06-19 16:00 ET to align on pilot scope — does that work for your team?

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, 14 Jun 2028 18:05:00 +0000 Jonas Weber wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed MAP...

Hi all —

Thanks, Jonas. Summary + what we’ll do from a technical qualification perspective:

A) Quick validation checklist (what we’ll test during pilot):
  - Baseline latency profile: synthetic and replayed streaming traces at 120 concurrent sessions
  - Token-generation P95/P99 under burst conditions (simulate client-side LB overhead + 2–3x user think-time)
  - Resource utilization: GPU memory + host CPU/RAM during steady state and ramp to 250 concurrent sessions
  - Recovery/fallback: verify automatic routing to a lower-cost variant if latency degrades past SLOs

B) Data we need from NovaMed (by EOD Mon if possible):
  - one-hour tcpdump or a sanitized NetFlow dump (zip) — filename: novamed-network-sample.trace.zip
  - representative prompt set and expected output length (spreadsheet is fine)
  - approximate percent of sessions that will be streaming vs short-turn requests (ballpark is OK)

C) Pilot runbook outline (deliverable):
  - Day 0: ingest traces and run replay to produce latency/throughput curve
  - Day 1: parameter tuning (batch size, KV cache windows, quantization profile suggestions)
  - Day 2: stress run to 250 sessions for 30 minutes and produce ops dashboard (token-level cost, latency histograms)

I’ll attach the preliminary MOP worksheet and a short checklist — Jonas, I’ll drop the MOP spreadsheet to the Drive link and share with Emma/Mark.

Questions for NovaMed: do you have a hard SLA requirement for P99 token latency or is P95 sufficient for now? Also what is your retention requirement for audit logs (we have options: 30/90/365 days)?

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (prelim MOP template)
From: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@novamed.com>

Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance readiness: MOP items and streaming constraints

Thanks Jonas and Karthik — great session. Quick replies inline.

- We can provide the network trace (sanitized) and a representative prompt set; attaching the trace and a short CSV of sample prompts now.
- Streaming vs short-turn split: roughly 55% streaming (live transcription sessions), 45% short-turn calls. Average streaming session is ~14s, keepalive 10s, median output tokens ~18.
- Concurrent users: alpha 120 concurrent; we typically expect spikes to 220 for short windows (approx 7–10 minutes).
- P99 requirement: for safety-critical UX we’d like P99 token latency <= 1.2s, but willing to accept a staged approach (P95 first, P99 as gating for GA).
- Audit logs: we need 90-day retention for the pilot.

We uploaded the trace as novamed-network-sample.trace.zip and sample_prompts_novamed.csv to the Drive link you shared.

Proposed next steps: confirm Tue 2028-06-19 16:00 ET for pilot scope and we’ll aim to get the traces to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Emma
